sentence.ja: さくらさん、{おはよう}。

mnemonic.story: Sunrise over an *Ohio* cornfield: the rooster on the fence crows "O-hi-o!" instead of cock-a-doodle-doo, and the whole farm yawns **good morning**. Ohayō: good morning, the casual one for friends and family.

sentence.ja: 先生[せんせい]、{おはようございます}。

mnemonic.story: Ohayō plus gozaimasu, a polite "it is". Your sleepy boss shuffles in with an *Ohio* mug, *goes* "*sigh*" and slumps onto the office *moss* while you bow: **good morning (polite)**. Ohayō gozaimasu: good morning.

sentence.ja: 田中[たなか]さん、{こんにちは}。

mnemonic.story: Midday sun: you wedge your dripping ice-cream *cone* into a stone *niche* in the wall, and a neighbour strolling past calls "*Wah*, **good afternoon**!" The last kana is written ha but said wa. Konnichiwa: good afternoon; also plain hello.

sentence.ja: 山田[やまだ]さん、{こんばんは}。

mnemonic.story: After dark the ice-cream *cone* is gone, so you swap it for a warm *bun* from a night stall, and the baker calls "*Wah*, **good evening**!" Noon is cone-niche, night is cone-bun. Konbanwa: good evening.

sentence.ja: みなさん、{さようなら}。

mnemonic.story: On the platform you *sigh*, "*Oh*, *Nora*," and wave **good-bye** as her train pulls away, the whistle fading into the hills. It sounds final, so friends who meet tomorrow often use something lighter. Sayōnara: good-bye.

sentence.ja: お父[とう]さん、{おやすみなさい}。

mnemonic.story: Yasumi means rest and nasai makes it a polite "please": please rest. Your cat sits on your pillow and glares; "*Oh ya*, *sue me*," you mumble, shoving it over and clicking off the lamp. **Good night**. Oyasumi (nasai): good night.

sentence.ja: お茶[ちゃ]、{ありがとう}。

mnemonic.story: An *alligator* slides out of the pond and drops your stolen sandal at your feet, slimy and dented. You say **thank you**, very carefully, while counting your toes. Arigatō: thank you, the casual one.

sentence.ja: お土産[みやげ]、{ありがとうございます}。

breakdown.text: ありがとうございます

mnemonic.story: This time the *alligator* returns your sandal polished and gift-wrapped, so plain thanks won't do. Add gozaimasu, the same polite tail as the morning greeting, and bow: **thank you (polite)**. Arigatō gozaimasu: thank you.

sentence.ja: {すみません}、今[いま]何時[なんじ]ですか。
sentence.en: Excuse me, what time is it?

mnemonic.story: Squeezing off a packed train, your backpack knocks a builder's hard hat crooked. "*Sue me*, *Mason*, **excuse me**!" you blurt as the doors hiss shut behind you. Sumimasen: excuse me; also I'm sorry.

sentence.ja: {ごめんなさい}、昨日[きのう]はアルバイトがありました。

mnemonic.story: You yell "*Go, men!*" and your relay team runs straight into a wall. "*Nah... sigh*." **I'm sorry**. Gomen-nasai: literally "pardon, please"; casual, for friends and family.

sentence.ja: {はじめまして}。山田[やまだ]です。
sentence.en: How do you do? I'm Yamada.

mnemonic.story: "*Ha*!" laughs a stranger named *Jimmy*, shaking your hand with fingers still green from the *mashed tea* he was whisking: **how do you do?** Hajimemashite: "for the first time", said only when you first meet.

sentence.ja: 田中[たなか]です。{よろしくお願[ねが]いします}。
sentence.en: I'm Tanaka. Nice to meet you.

breakdown.text: よろしくお願いします

mnemonic.story: "*Yo*!" A *rosy*-cheeked pigeon struts up, bows and *coos* yoroshiku, "please be kind to me". Onegaishimasu, "I ask of you", makes it polite. Together, **nice to meet you**. Yoroshiku onegaishimasu: nice to meet you.

sentence.ja: じゃあ、{いってきます}。
sentence.en: Right, I'm off. See you later.

mnemonic.story: Itte means go and kimasu means come. On your way out you step over your *techie* roommate, asleep on the *moss*-green rug among cables, and call **I'll go and come back**. Ittekimasu: said by the one leaving home.

sentence.ja: ケンさん、{いってらっしゃい}。
sentence.en: Have a good day, Ken. See you when you're back.

mnemonic.story: Your grandmother leans over the *terrace* railing and gives a *shy* little wave as you set off: **please go and come back**. Itterasshai: said by whoever stays home; the one leaving says ittekimasu.

sentence.ja: お母[かあ]さん、{ただいま}。

mnemonic.story: You kick the front door open, fling your arms wide and announce "*Ta-da*, *I'm*... **home**!" to a hallway that smells of curry. Tadaima: I'm home.

sentence.ja: 「ただいま。」「{おかえり}。」

mnemonic.story: Kaeri means return. Your mum meets you at the door, grabs your heavy bag with "*Oh*, *carry*? Give it here," and steers you inside: **welcome home**. Okaeri (nasai): the reply to tadaima.

sentence.ja: では、{いただきます}。

breakdown.en: thank you for the meal (before eating)

mnemonic.story: "*Eee*, *ta-da*!" The lid comes off the bubbling hotpot, steam fogs your glasses, and everyone presses their palms together: **thank you for the meal**. Itadakimasu: literally "I humbly receive", said before the first bite.

sentence.ja: 田中[たなか]さん、{ごちそうさまでした}。
sentence.en: Thank you for the meal, Mr. Tanaka.

breakdown.en: thank you for the meal (after eating)

mnemonic.story: You *go* for the last *cheese* wedge, *so* the *summer* picnic is officially over; chopsticks down, hands together: **thank you for the meal (after eating)**. Gochisōsama (deshita): literally "it was a feast".

sentence.ja: {もしもし}、田中[たなか]さんですか。

mnemonic.story: You ring the farm, ask "**Hello?**", and the farmer just yells "*Mo' sheep, mo' sheep!*" over the baaing. Moshi-moshi: hello, only on the phone.

sentence.ja: 田中[たなか]さん、{久[ひさ]しぶり}ですね。
sentence.en: Tanaka-san, it's been a long time!

breakdown.en: it has been a long time

mnemonic.story: "Look, *he sashays*!" Your old friend glides in after years away with a wheel of *Brie*: **it's been a long time**. Hisashi is a long while, buri after a gap. Hisashi-buri.

sentence.ja: 「風邪[かぜ]をひきました。」「{お大事[だいじ]に}。」

mnemonic.story: Literally 'preciously': o, daiji (precious), ni. A *dye genie* swirls out of the medicine bottle, wraps your friend in a warm purple blanket and whispers, '**Get well soon**.' O-daiji ni.

sentence.ja: ケンさんの誕生日[たんじょうび]に{乾杯[かんぱい]}！

mnemonic.story: Kan is dry and pai is cup: dry your cup. Everyone clinks *cans* above a birthday *pie*, foam dripping onto the crust, and shouts **Cheers!** Kanpai.

sentence.ja: 「日本人[にほんじん]ですか。」「{はい}、日本人[にほんじん]です。」

mnemonic.story: The teacher calls your name and you shoot an arm up: "*Hi!*" In Japanese that means **yes**, present, here. Hai: a formal yes, not a greeting.

sentence.ja: 「学生[がくせい]ですか。」「{いいえ}、先生[せんせい]です。」
sentence.en: "Are you a student?" "No, I'm a teacher."

mnemonic.story: A salesman wedges his foot in your door; you lean on it and the rusty hinges squeal a long *eee-eh* as it shuts. That squeal is **no**. Iie: no; also "not at all" when someone thanks or apologises.

sentence.ja: {ええ}、いいですよ。

mnemonic.story: Mouth full of noodles, you can only nod and hum a long "*ehh*" when your friend asks if they're good: **yes**. Ē is a soft yes; iie is no.

sentence.ja: 「明日[あした]、来[く]る？」「{うん}、行[い]く。」

mnemonic.story: Mouth full of noodles, you nod and grunt one short *oon*: a **yes** so lazy it is barely a word. Hai is for teachers; un is for friends. Un: uh-huh, yes.

sentence.ja: 「コーヒー、飲[の]む？」「{ううん}、いらない。」

mnemonic.story: Shake your head and hum two beats, *oo-oon*, the second one dipping: a friendly **no**. Un is one beat and means yes, so count the beats. Uun: uh-uh, no.

sentence.ja: 「ケンさんですか。」「はい、{そうです}。」

mnemonic.story: Sō means so and desu means it is: "It is *so*." A quiz host slaps the buzzer, ding: **That's right**. Sō desu.

sentence.ja: 「十九歳[じゅうきゅうさい]です。」「{そうですか}。」

mnemonic.story: Sō desu plus ka, a question: "Is it so?" Let your voice sink like a slow nod, *sō desu ka*..., and it means **I see**. Said rising, it turns into surprise.

sentence.ja: {どうぞ}、私[わたし]の傘[かさ]です。

mnemonic.story: A bull*dozer* rumbles to a stop at the crossing and the driver waves you across: **please**, after you. Dōzo: please; also here it is.

sentence.ja: 「これ、どうぞ。」「あ、{どうも}。」

mnemonic.story: The baker slips extra *dough* into your bag, "*more*?", and you bow twice: **thank you**. Dōmo: thank you.

sentence.ja: {あのう}、留学生[りゅうがくせい]ですか。
sentence.en: Um, are you an international student?

mnemonic.story: You tap a stranger on the shoulder, "*Ah, no*...", then lose your nerve and just hover there: **um...** Anō, the long ō a polite way to stall before a question.

sentence.ja: {じゃあ}、これをお願[ねが]いします。
sentence.en: Then I'll have this one, please.

mnemonic.story: The shop is out of bags? **Then** you'll carry the honey home in the sticky *jar*, cradled in both hands. Jā: then; if that's the case.

sentence.ja: 「雨[あめ]ですよ。」「{大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]}です。傘[かさ]があります。」
sentence.en: "It's raining." "It's okay. I have an umbrella."

mnemonic.story: You knock a bucket of *dye* over *Joe*. He rises dripping purple, says "*Boo!*", and laughs: **it's okay**, no harm done. Daijōbu: it's okay, not to worry.

sentence.ja: 「明日[あした]テストがありますよ。」「えっ、{本当[ほんとう]ですか}。」

mnemonic.story: Hontō is the truth; desu ka makes "is that the truth?": **Really?** A friend swears they *hone* each *toe*nail on a knife sharpener, grinding sparks. "Hontō desu ka?"

sentence.ja: 「明日[あした]、来[き]ますか。」「{もちろん}行[い]きます。」
sentence.en: "Are you coming tomorrow?" "Of course I'll be there."

mnemonic.story: A midnight *mochi run* to the corner shop? **Of course**. You're already pulling on your shoes, sweet rice powder still on your fingers from the last batch. Mochiron: of course.
